newsitem.title: USA: Sanluis sees earns hurt by expansion costs.
newsitem.headline: Sanluis sees earns hurt by expansion costs.

text.p: Mexico's Sanluis Corporacion SA de CV expects to see its earnings weighed down late this year by expansion costs at its auto parts plants, the company's investor relations manager said Wednesday.

The executive, Hector Amador, told an Smith Barney sponsored investor conference that Sanluis would start to make truck suspensions in 1998 in a joint venture with Hendrickson and expand its production of suspensions and brakes.
"We'll start feeling the impact in the fouth quarter of this year," he said.
However Amador said Sanluis should start to generate revenue from the new production starting in January 1998.
"Beginning in January you'll begin to feel the benefits," he said.

Sanluis has a contract to supply brakes and suspensions to General Motors Corp and suspensions to Ford Motor Corp. Amador did not comment on how the increased costs, including $15 million for the truck suspension plant, would affect its earnings per share.
